programmes.d: In this classic episode of Forensic Files, the longest-running true crime series in television history, Eileen and Derrick Severs disappear from their home in a small village in Great Britain and police find evidence of foul play.
A talented television news anchor is shot to death outside her home.
The victim had ingested a massive amount of cyanide. An unlikely clue — a flaw on a mailing envelope — exposed a murderer who was willing to kill innocent people.
A woman is haunted by the memory of her father murdering her mother.
The decomposed body of a young woman was discovered in a Bakersfield irrigation canal. If there was trace evidence, it had been washed away.
When a successful stockbroker doesn't return home after a late shift, his wife reports him missing.
When a hit-and-run boating accident caused the death of a popular young man, investigators faced the daunting task of searching for one boat among 1200 others.
Police investigate the shooting of a homicide detective's wife.

Between 1985 and 1988, 18 people were choked, molested and left for dead in the remote mountains of California. The only witnesses were the insects — and they play an important role in solving the crimes and bringing the killer to justice.
A woman, who had recently rejected a co-worker half her age, ends up dead in her driveway.
When the body of a young woman is found under an isolated highway ramp, a unique fiber on the victim's clothing leads San Diego police straight to the most unlikely of killers.
New York police hunt the Zodiac killer after a series of deadly attacks.
A 16-year-old girl is killed in her own home by her parents, who claim they acted in self-defense.

California police had several suspects in the robbery and brutal murder of an elderly couple. Ten years later, a determined forensic scientist used material from a dentist's office to uncover ballistic evidence that had been overlooked.
In 2004, Mary Ann Clibbery was found brutally murdered in her Illinois business.
For six years, a serial killer prowled the streets of New York City. He wrote letters to police and The New York Post, indicating he would kill twelve people — one for each astrological sign.
In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with $500,000 in gold coins.

In the early hours of a morning just before Christmas, a college student was abducted from the parking lot of her apartment. Her body was found later that day; she had been sexually assaulted and shot at point-blank range.
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
Aspiring model's death points to her boyfriend who is soon cleared.

In 1991, San Francisco pornographer Artie Mitchell was murdered in his home. His brother and business partner, who was found near the scene carrying a rifle, later confesses to shooting Artie.The question is whether the shooting was premeditated.
The prime suspect's driver's license was found at the scene of a brutal double homicide.
After shooting his victims in the head, the killer staged the scene, placed the incriminating evidence into a plastic bag and tossed it into the river.
A painstaking investigation leads police to a lawyer husband with a motive to kill his wife.

When Kristine Fitzhugh failed to show up for her music class, her husband found her dead at the bottom of the stairs of their Palo Alto home. Further investigation reveals evidence of murder in the kitchen.
The body of a young woman is found under an isolated highway ramp.

A mysterious computer crash pushed a thriving manufacturing company to the brink of collapse, jeopardizing hundreds of employees' jobs. Forensic investigators must determine if the crash was the result of a computer defect, human error or sabotage.
An examination of the 2002 DC area shooting spree that resulted in ten murders.
Who was the sexual offender who murdered two adolescent boys in Nebraska? The key to stopping him would be the unique composition of the "junk rope" he used to tie his victims.
A woman and her soon-to-be ex-husband are murdered shortly after she meets a man online.
How did the stalker obtain the security system code for his victim's home? How did he steal her personal photographs? Police needed answers and they found them in the most unlikely of places.
A high school gym teacher mysteriously leaves town without saying goodbye to anyone.

In the summer of 1986, Kathleen Lipscomb's body was found on a deserted road outside of San Antonio. Months and years passed, but the crime was never solved. Finally, a private investigator discovered Kathleen's diary.
Even though their daughter had run away before, she'd always come back.
When police recovered the submerged car of a missing man, they expected to find his body — but it wasn't there. The investigation that followed would uncover an obsession turned deadly.
Soon after becoming pregnant, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates.
Police are dispatched to the scene of a shooting and discover the victim's husband is one of their own: a homicide detective who says his wife accidentally shot herself in the head.
In 1984, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement that bars have video cameras installed on the premises.
Police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife.

In 1980, Michigan resident Shannon Mohr died in what her new husband, David Davis, reported to be a horseback riding accident. After her death, Shannon's family reported that Davis seemed far from grief-stricken.
A serial killer was strangling prostitutes in Florida then leaving the bodies in plain sight.
In 2008, the body of Colorado real estate developer Alan Helmick was found by his wife, Miriam, who then became the prime suspect.
A family vacation turns into a nightmare when the wife is found face-down in the lake.
In 2004, Rebecca Barney and her soon-to-be ex-husband Fred were found shot to death in their Tulsa, Oklahoma, home, which had been set on fire.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.

A 29-year-old woman is killed instantly when a bomb explodes in her home. The device is so powerful that it embedded shrapnel in houses across the street. The bomber had not only knowledge and skill, but also a motive for murder.
Police charge a mentally unstable man with his wife's murder even though she died of natural causes.
In 1985, Julie Estes was kidnapped from the Southside convenience store where she worked. Her body was found the next day, but the killing went unsolved until 2003.
Ten bodies had been found between May and November 1984 in Florida.
While skeet shooting on a beautiful spring day, Martin Dillon is shot dead. His friend maintains it was a freak accident, but it takes more than 20 years for the truth to surface.
A mother with Munchausen syndrome by proxy kills one child and physically abuses another.
In 1995, Palm Beach waitress Denise O'Neill is abducted and murdered. Her neighbor Luis Caballero arouses suspicions by behaving oddly toward TV crews covering the crime.
Investigators sift through the ashes of a fire which killed a 40-year-old woman.

When Leann Fletcher is found dead, investigators use blood spatter analysis and forensic computing to find a motive for her murder: her husband, a prominent lawyer, was having an affair with judge Susan Chrzanowski.
The 1987 disappearance of Houston resident Tracy Jo Shine is recalled.
A woman is haunted by the memory of her father murdering her mother.
In 2006, Darlene VanderGiesen received threatening emails and then disappeared. Tracking the source of the emails led police to the home of Daphne Wright, where they believe a murder was committed.
Mark Fair left for work and his fiancée, Karla Brown, stayed home. Later, he found her dead. During the autopsy, bite marks on her body were re-examined and forensic odontology identified the killer.
A small community is devastated when a car accident claims the life of a well-respected nurse.
Heavy rains and snow run-off carried manure into Milwaukee's water supply in 1993.
In 2000, teenager Tara Munsey went missing after a work shift at a Virginia restaurant. Did she run away, or was she the victim of foul play?
Police charge a mentally unstable man with his wife's murder even though she died of natural causes.
The body of 16-year-old Leanne Tiernan was discovered nine months after she disappeared. Forensic scientists found clues that painted a virtual portrait of her killer.
A tiny clue inside a suspect's watchband and a popular television show help solve a case.

A woman was brutally murdered in her home and the only witnesses to the crime were the family dogs. An expert in canine behavior was convinced the killer knew both the victim and the animals, and he was determined find out what the dogs had seen.
A man vows to find the person responsible for the death of his sister.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas. Later, a fourth murder from the same time period provided the police with far more than they realized.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.

A suspect's former lover comes forward with a fantastic tale of murder, mutilation and cremation. But there's no way to test the story's validity — until a plant pathologist and a dendrochronologist conduct tests where the cremation supposedly occurred.
Respected surgeon is stabbed to death. However the key suspect has a solid alibi.
At the scene of a vicious murder, the killer went to a great deal of effort to wipe away his fingerprints and obscure his shoe impressions left when he tracked blood trails on the floor.
When a pipe bomb ripped through a rural home, police had no idea who was responsible.

In 1999, Susan Fassett was gunned down as she left her church choir practice in Poughkeepsie, NY. After clearing her husband, police turned their attention to Fred Andros, with whom Susan had an affair.
When an unsolved murder is reopened, a listen to the 911 call determines the murderer and motive.

Investigators are baffled after finding a murder scene devoid of any physical evidence, but they suspect that the victim's dog had witnessed the crime. If so, forensic scientists would have to find some way to learn what the dog had seen.
911 received a call from a man who said his girlfriend shot herself. The autopsy revealed the truth.

A woman who was known to have suffered from depression apparently took her own life. But her sister told police that, a year before her death, she said if anything were to happen to her there would be a note in the china cabinet.
Security cameras in a casino tracked a woman's movements until right before she disappeared.
In 2000, Judy Southern arrived home from work and was shot by a gunman waiting within. Her husband arrived shortly afterwards, called emergency services and drove her to the hospital.
Old-fashioned police work and computer animation determine how a 15-year-old boy was shot.

In little more than a month, two women who lived in the same apartment complex were brutally murdered. The similarities of the crime scenes led police to conclude they were dealing with a serial killer who harbored an intense hatred of women.
In this case, it looked like the killer vanished into thin air...and perhaps he had.
For 15 months, a serial killer was strangling prostitutes in Florida, then taunting police by leaving the bodies in plain sight. The only clues were a tire impression and some threads.
Seattle police had no suspects in the murder of a post-grunge singer for more than a decade.
When a young fireman died from what appeared to be serious but undiagnosed heart disease, his family and friends had no proof of foul play.
Three homicides on two continents have investigators on both sides of the Atlantic puzzled.
Tara Munsey went missing after a work shift at a Virginia restaurant.

In 1984, California firefighters battled ten arson fires in three weeks. When cigarettes and a scrap of paper connected the case to similar fires further north, the hunt was on for a dangerous pyromaniac.
A young woman attends evening church services... then disappears.
In 2003, St. Cloud teenager Jason MacLennan returned home after a night out with friends and discovered his father's body lying in a pool of blood.
A behavioral profile caused the Baton Rouge Police Department to search for the wrong man.

Nancy Newman and her two daughters are found brutally murdered. The crime scene has no shortage of evidence, but investigators cannot find a conclusive link to their prime suspect. To solve the puzzle, an FBI analyst designs a unique experiment.
A clue no bigger than a thumbtack leads investigators to a trio of killers.
In the 1990s, the media dubbed Richard Rogers the "Last Call Killer" because he targeted men in gay bars who were obviously intoxicated.
In 1995, Palm Beach waitress Denise O'Neill is abducted and murdered.
While investigating the apparent overdose suicide of Reverend Bill Guthrie's wife, detectives recover incriminating files from Bill's computer and learn of his infidelity.
A young girl with no ID is found on an isolated farm but has mailbox and house keys.
